A dashcam writes continuously — as long as it is recording, it is writing.

Flash memory has a limited write endurance. Using the head unit's internal storage as the dashcam's destination will measurably consume that endurance, and this storage usually cannot be replaced.

A USB drive is recommended: it can be swapped when it wears out, and pulled out to copy files off.

A surround-view dashcam for Zeekr head units: it records the vehicle\'s 360° composite stream and adds playback, a super mirror and more.

Recordings are written to external storage only, never to the head unit's internal flash — a dashcam writes continuously, and that storage cannot be replaced once worn out.

• The USB drive supplied with the car is enough for basic recording.

• For a higher bitrate or a longer retention window without occupying the original drive, add a second one through the left-hand Type-C port. The head unit picks it up automatically and it can be removed at any time.

• Verified working: a 128 GB USB drive; an NVMe SSD (far faster, which largely removes the write bottleneck, though it runs warmer).

• Optane-based M10 drives are good value, but their capacity is small — roughly the last 20 hours.
⚠ Recordings on the USB drive are not encrypted. The drive can be removed and read on any other device, so treat privacy accordingly.

This app is released under the GNU GPL v3.0, inherited from EVCam by suyunkai — the camera, recording and floating-window foundations come from it.

That Zeekr head units expose a single pre-composited surround stream (rather than four separate cameras), along with its layout and rendering constraints, was first documented publicly by AVM Recorder by Dantenothing. That project reserves all rights; no code from it has been copied here — only the factual conclusions drawn from its public material. With thanks.
